evidence: RULE 1: a MEASURED offset must exist as its OWN ROW. Recording a measurement inside another row's evidence prose does not reach the resolver. Rows starting with # are skipped by jlc_rotation_resolve.py.

RULE 2 (2026-07-25, THE CORRECTION BELOW): NEVER populate a row from jlc_twin's jlc_offset. Derive it from the BOARD + JLC's cached model with an operator VERIFIED against pcbnew itself (pad.GetFPRelativePosition() vs pad.GetPosition()). jlc_twin.xform() used the wrong handedness, so every offset it reported was NEGATED: invisible at 0/180 (sign-invariant) and exactly 180deg wrong at 90/270. Six rows here were populated from it and were all 180deg wrong. Checker and checked must not share a method (canon M1).

RULE 3 (2026-07-25, canon A-POL): the `polarity` column is a REQUIRED DECLARATION, one of n/a | two-channel | single-channel. A pad-NUMBER fit structurally CANNOT detect a model whose own numbering differs from ours, and a HIGH FIT MARGIN IS NOT CONFIDENCE: on usb-hub-3s-v3's indicator LEDs (C2296/C2297) the pad-number fit returns 180 with a 17.7x margin and is WRONG — JLC numbers pad 1 = ANODE while KiCad Device:LED is pin 1 = K, both libraries draw the cathode WEST, so the true offset is 0 and a 180 row would ship every indicator dark (indistinguishable from a bad joint). two-channel = a NUMBERING-FREE channel (silk chamfer, pin-1 dot/glyph, mounting-tab position, body/courtyard asymmetry, lead axis) is RECORDED IN THIS ROW. single-channel = no such channel exists; the row MUST name the JLC order-preview human gate, which then carries it before first order. Graded by jlc_rotation_audit.py --table.
